Aimed at letting users and future features (like periodic rebroadcast until confirmation) introspect and reuse this metadata.

why: P3 because it adds new fields (received_by_us address/time) to getprivatebroadcastinfo, giving external tooling visibility they previously lost once a tx was received back (vasild).
No external consumer has asked for this specific field; value is speculative diagnostic tooling rather than a reported pain point.

result.summary: This PR changes the private broadcast module so that transactions received back from the network stay in the in-memory queue (marked as no longer pending) instead of being removed, and records which peer they were received from and when. The getprivatebroadcastinfo RPC now surfaces this as a received_by_us object with address and time. To bound memory, the queue evicts the oldest non-pending transaction when at the existing 10,000-transaction cap (from prior PR #35406).
result.problem: Previously, once a privately-broadcast transaction was received back from the network, all metadata about it (who it was sent to, when, who returned it) was discarded, so users and tooling built on getprivatebroadcastinfo could not distinguish 'never broadcast', 'successfully broadcast', or 'broadcast but node restarted' states, and could not audit round-trip timing.

open_concerns: instagibbs's concept NACK (2026-09-02, reiterated 2026-09-09) that the feature adds scope/complexity for a niche use case and that private broadcast should not become a general rebroadcast/introspection mechanism; he also disputes the author's claim that this closes a timing-attack privacy leak from #29415, and the thread ended without agreement, with instagibbs stepping back rather than retracting.
optout21's 2026-09-15 comment that the eviction `if` (not `while`) does not guarantee the queue stays under the cap after insertion, still open as of the latest activity.
resolved_concerns: vasild's suggestion to separate 'in mempool' / 'acceptable' / 'rejected' states was implemented via an enum, simplifying the logic (andrewtoth).
vasild's and rkrux's naming/structure nits (TxSendStatus->TxBroadcastStatus, received->received_by_us, GetPendingTransactions removal) were addressed.
danielabrozzoni's point about time_added not being reset on re-Add was fixed and covered by a unit test.
instagibbs's memory-growth/DoS concern was addressed by a separate merged PR (#35406) capping the queue at 10,000 entries, which this PR now builds on for eviction.
instagibbs's double-decrement correctness concern on attempts_remaining was fixed (set to 0 once received).

result.card: This PR changes the private-broadcast module so transactions received back from the network stay in the in-memory queue with recorded peer/time metadata instead of being deleted, and surfaces that via a new received_by_us field on the getprivatebroadcastinfo RPC, evicting the oldest finished entry once the existing 10,000-tx cap is hit. It targets private-broadcast users and tooling that currently lose all visibility into a transaction once it round-trips back to the node, and is pitched by the author as a stepping stone toward a node-driven rebroadcast-until-confirmed feature requested in issue #30471 and pursued further in open PR #34322. Three members (vasild, optout21, danielabrozzoni) ACKed after several review rounds, while instagibbs raised a concept NACK questioning whether the feature's value justifies the added complexity and disputing the author's claim that it closes a related timing-attack privacy leak; the disagreement was aired at length but not formally resolved, with instagibbs stepping back to let others weigh in. The code itself is currently reviewable, with only minor nits open as of the latest activity (2026-09-15). No hard external dependency blocks this PR; it depends conceptually on nothing merged but sets up #34322.
